concept.title: All projects, and links between them

conbody.p: All projects shows the plan of every project of the workspace that you can read, each on a line with its tasks, its milestones and its progress. Level, beside the Project heading, sets how far down the tasks go: Level 1, which it opens on until you choose another (your browser remembers the choice), is each project's top-level tasks, each level further adds the sub-tasks beneath their parents, whose bars stay as they do on the Gantt, and All levels goes all the way down. Milestones show at every level. The bars are the Gantt's own: green when done, red when late, filled as far as the work has gone, and a parent in grey. Each project's critical path is the top row of its line. The lines share one time scale and scroll sideways together, while the projects' names stay in place. A project's name opens its Gantt. A project that belongs under another is listed beneath it, indented, and the arrow beside a parent's name folds its projects away. The same chart has a page of its own that belongs to no project: Plan, in the workspace's menu beside Home, with its own Critical path, Today and time scale.

A task can wait on a task of another project of the same workspace. In the task's panel, under Other projects, choose Wait on a task of another project, then the project, the task, the relationship and an offset. The task then follows the other one when the plan is recalculated, or at once on an automatic plan. The other project's task is never moved from here, and it is not a row of this plan: it is named on the task it is linked to, in both projects, where two joined rings beside the task's name mark the link (red when the dates break it; ⇄ before the name on the Timeline and All projects), and under Links between projects in All projects. A link whose dates are broken is marked.
